response.rationale: R1 uniquely matches the full constellation of facial dysmorphism, limb contractures, and femoral aplasia/hypoplasia, which is characteristic of the named syndrome. R4 only explains oligohydramnios-related limb shortening but not the specific facial and skeletal anomalies.

rejected.why: Only micrognathia and cleft lip/palate are shared; lacks femoral and other systemic findings.
Only abruptio placentae is cited; does not account for the specific congenital anomalies.
Oligohydramnios sequence is a general mechanism but fails to explain the distinctive facial and femoral features.
